indicator_assessments.name: PC / smartphone / server demand cuts
indicator_assessments.description: IDC, Counterpoint, Gartner revise forecasts down (the quantity signal) PLUS the leading price-pass-through edge — OEMs raising end-device prices or cutting memory content to offset memory costs.
indicator_assessments.what_to_look_for: QUANTITY (firing condition, already met): IDC PC shipment forecast revised to -5% or worse for 2026 (current -2.4 to -11.3% — already fired). Counterpoint smartphone <0% (current -2%). Gartner data center server forecast cut. LEADING / INTENSIFICATION (signal already fired — these DEEPEN it, they are the early end-market tell before forecast cuts widen): OEMs raising end-device prices to offset memory costs (Apple, Microsoft, Sony, Nintendo, Dell, Valve), removing low-spec/entry configurations, cutting memory content per device, substituting cheaper nodes, or delaying refresh cycles. NOTE: holding a price point by cutting memory content AND raising price to hold content are BOTH demand-destruction mechanisms — do not read a memory-content INCREASE (e.g. iPhone to 12GB for on-device AI) as a reversal; the destruction shows up in unit demand and price elasticity.

No OEM production restoration or forecast upgrade in today's feed. No intensification evidence (OEM price pass-through, memory-content cuts) in today's news. Signal holds on quarterly persistence.

indicator_assessments.name: DRAM Price Evolution (spot + contract matrix)
indicator_assessments.description: 5x5 trigger matrix mapping DRAM contract QoQ growth (rows) against DDR5 16Gb 4800/5600 spot drawdown from rolling 12-week peak (cols). Returns Not fired / Partially fired / Fired per cell. Replaces the v3.39 absolute-threshold trigger ($38.2 spot / $950 module). The matrix is the framework's canonical early-warning signal — spot drawdown leads contract direction by 6-10 weeks. Matrix engine: src/data/cycle_matrix.py; charts: src/analysis/chart_generator.py.
indicator_assessments.what_to_look_for: Today's cell position on the 5x5 matrix. ROWS (contract QoQ): R1 >=+30%, R2 +20-30%, R3 +10-20%, R4 +5-10%, R5 <=+5%. COLS (spot drawdown from rolling 12w peak): C1 at peak, C2 <5% off, C3 5-10% off, C4 10-20% off, C5 >=20% off. Not fired = R1/R2 with low drawdown (full position). Partially fired = mid-band (review thesis, consider 25-33% trim). Fired = any R4-R5 row, any C5 column, or R3+C4. Historical cycle peaks all landed in R5 by the time contract growth hit ~0% — the matrix exists to act BEFORE that. Contract row uses a SYNTHETIC estimate: anchor (most recent TrendForce quarterly forecast, preferring server_ddr5 > conventional_dram_aggregate segments) + 0.4 * tone_adj + 0.4 * supplier_adj + 0.2 * spot_lead_adj, each capped +/-30pp.
indicator_assessments.where_we_stand: Cell: Not fired (Row 1 x Col 1). No firing condition met — hold full position. DDR5 16Gb 4800/5600 spot $50.93 (2026-07-28 print). Contract anchor: Q2_2026 58-63% QoQ (trendforce_press_release, published 2026-03-31, 119d old). Synthetic adjusted: 50.8% central (range 48-53%). Adjustments: tone +3.3pp (9 src, weight 0.4); supplier -30.0pp (1 src, weight 0.4); spot_lead +5.0pp (1 src, weight 0.2).

indicator_assessments.what_to_look_for: Layoffs, workforce/headcount reductions, or fab idling/utilization cuts IN THE MEMORY OPERATIONS (DRAM/NAND/HBM lines, memory fabs, the memory/DS-Memory division) of Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, or other memory makers. For pure-play memory makers (SK Hynix, Micron) company-level cuts count — they ARE the memory business. If the affected business unit is not identified as memory/semiconductor-memory, do NOT fire. 'Samsung announces layoffs' alone is NEVER sufficient — the report must explicitly state the cuts hit memory operations/employees.
